REPLY BRIEF OF NARUNA INVESTMENTS, LLC, SCOTT’S ALAMO, LP,
SUSAN CORNWELL AND W. REEGAN BUSBY

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

I. SUMMARY OF REPLY

The closing briefs confirm Intervenors Naruna Investments, LLC, Scott’s Alamo, L.P.,
Susan Comwell and W. Reegan Busby’s (Naruna Intervenors) position rather than undermine it:
the Administrative Law Judges should reject Segment U1 (Link U1) and recommend any
otherwise-adequate filed route that avoids it. Nothing in any party’s initial brief gives the Public
Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) a reason to route the proposed transmission line
(Project) across Segment U1. Rather, the closing briefs that attack Oncor Electric Delivery
Company, LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s (Applicants) preferred best meets
Route 894 only sharpen the point that every route other parties urge as a substitute for Route 894
in the northern corridor necessarily includes Segment U1. This Reply mainly focuses on the
closing briefs of those parties urging routes with Segment U1 - 4K Land and Cattle Company (4K),
Solana Ranch Company, Solana Development, LP, Don A! Ringler, and CEDON Realty, Ltd.
(Solana Intervenors), Wulff Bluff Creek Ranch, Ltd. and Abell Ranches, Ltd. (Brady Creek
Intervenors) and Staten Creek Ranch.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
Naruna Intervenors’ Reply Brief — Page 1 of 7

 4K asks the ALJs to reject both Route 894 and Staff's preferred Route 487 in favor of
“Northern Corridor” routes. However, each of the ten routes 4K endorses (Routes 416, 410, 392,
402, 391, 589, 592, 74, 93, and 100) includes Segment U1 that would bisect the 120-year old
Naruna ranch. Solana and Brady Creek Intervenors urge Route 392, which likewise includes
Segment U1. The contest those parties have framed is therefore not “Route 894 versus a better
route.” It is “a non-U1 route versus Segment U1.” On that question the record is one-sided: the
Applicants’ routing engineer selected a non-U]1 route, Staff selected anon-U] route, and no party
defends Segment U1 on its merits which would result in a longer and more expensive northern

route. Commission Staff’s preferred Route 487—and 98 other filed routes —avoid Segment U1 n

The Naruna Intervenors do not ask the ALJs to recommend Route 894, to resolve the
disputesamong the route proponents, or to grant any landowneran outlier accommodation. Ninety -
eight filed routes avoid Segment U1. The ALJs need only decline to select the inferior segment
that the Applicants’ and Staffs own choices already avoid.

I. ARGUMENT

A. Reply to 4K

4K’s “Northern Corridor” only spares its own ranch but would route the line across the
Naruna Intervenors’ ranch instead. 4K opposes both Route 894 and Staff's Route 487 because
each “utilize[s] links that would cross the 4K Ranch”-—specifically Links M12, M11, K52, and
K51.2 To avoid those links, 4K asks the Commission to select a “Northern Corridor” route,
identifying Routes 416, 410, 392, 402, 391, 589, 592, 74, 93, and 100.3 Every one of those ten
routes includes Segment U1.4 More disturbingly, each would lay a 765-kV line diagonally across
the Naruna ranch for roughly 1.17 miles, across the KWSC public water infrastructure, and within
500 feet of the habitable structures identified in the Cornwell Direct.> 4K’s brief does not mention
Segment U1, the KWSC water system, or the U1 habitable structures and it offers no analysis of
the segment’s paralleling performance. 4K’s position relocates the burden of the line from its own

ranch onto the Naruna Intervenors’ ranch and onto every other Segment U1 landowner. The

' Ex. SC-11.

2? 4K Land and Cattle Company’s Initial Brief at 6—7.

3 Jd. at 7; 4K Land Ex. 4, King Cross Rebuttal at 1-2; 4K Land Ex. 1, Scott Direct at 175-178.
4 Petty Direct, Ex. CDP-6, Tbl. 1; Oncor & LCRA TSC Ex. 1 at 2780-2781; Ex. SC-11.

5 Comwell Direct §§ V, VII, IX; Ex. SC-2, SC-3A, SC-7.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
Naruna Intervenors’ Reply Brief — Page 2 of 7

 routing statute does not permit one landowner’s preference to be satisfied by shifting the line onto

a corridor that performs worse on the very factors the Commission must weigh.®

The corridor 4K prefers is, as shown by the Applicants’ own data, the worst paralleling
performer in the filing. Segment U1 appears in only 24 of the 122 filed routes (19.7%) but in 15
of the 20 worst-performing routes ranked by paralleling percentage (75%). Additionally, the
northem Link U6 corridor—the corridor that includes Segment U1—parallels existing compatible
right-of-way for only 29.1% to 44.6% of route length which is the lowest band of the five filed
corridors.’ Thus, 4K’s preference for the Northern Corridor is a preference for the corridor that
least satisfies the Section 25.101(b)(3)(B) paralleling factor.

4K’s “weighted -scoring” attack on Route 894 also supplies no basis to prefer Segment U1,
and is not supported by Commission practice. 4K’s contention that Route 894 is deficient rests
entirely on Mr. Scott’s weighted-scoring model, under which Route 894 “ranks 83rd.”8 However,
as former Commissioner-experts testified, routing is not decided by a scoring formula. That is,
route selection is “not amath question” but “a balancing of factors.”? On the other hand, a granular
scoring analysis “would be in the eye of the beholder” and “is subjective.”!° Commission Staffs
own engineer agreed his recommendation rested on professional judgment, not a formula.!! 4K’s

model cannot displace the statutory balancing the Commission is required to perform.

Second, and dispositively for the Naruna Intervenors, 4K’s scoring critique—even if
credited in full—is an argument against Route 894 and not an argument for Segment U1.
Discrediting Route 894 would, at most, point the Commission toward Route 487 or another non-
U1 route. It would never point toward Segment U1. The routes 4K’s model would substitute are
the same U1 routes that carry up to 136 habitable structures and the worst paralleling performance
in the filing.

6 PURA § 37.056(cX4); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)3\B).

7 Ex. SC-25; Petty Direct, Ex. CDP-6 at 42, Tbls. 1-2.

8 4K Initial Brief at 8, 12.

9 Tr. Vol. 5 at 163:17—19 (Smitherman) (June 11, 2026).

10 Tr, Vol. 6 at 76:25, 77:16—-19 (McAdams) (June 12, 2026).

11 Tr, Vol. 4 at 87:8-23 (Poole) (June 10, 2026)); See also, Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 41.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
Naruna Intervenors’ Reply Brief — Page 3 of 7

 B. Reply to Applicants and 4K

“Every filed route is acceptable” is the floor, not the standard and the Commission must
select the route that best meets the criteria, and no party contends that a Segment U1 route does.
Yet, the Applicants and 4K both rely on the Applicants’ concession that “[alny of those 122 routes
are viable and constructible.”!2 The Naruna Intervenors do not dispute that concession—they rely
on it. But “viable and constructible” is the threshold every filed route must clear; it is not the
decision standard. PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) require the Commission
to weigh the statutory factors and select the route that best meets them. A route may be lawful to
build and still be the wrong route to choose.

On that decisional question, no party in this record contends that any Segment U1 route
best meets the criteria. The Applicants identified non-U1 Route 89413 while Commission Staff
identified non-U1 Route 487.!4 Even the parties opposing Route 894 do not defend Segment U1.
For example, Save the Lampasas urges non-U1 Routes 296 and 572!° and the U3 Landowners who
are situated on the very link the Segment U1 routes use to reach the Colorado River reject every
U3 route and urge Route 894.16 The concession that all routes are “acceptable” cannot convert the

worst-paralleling, least-supported segment into the best route.

Cc. Reply to Solana and Brady Creek Intervenors

The Solana and Brady Creek Intervenors’ affirmative case for Route 392 collapses on the
proponents’ own evidence. The only Segment U1 route any party affirmatively advocatesis Route
392. First, the case for Route 392 depends entirely on a threshold “Link U3” screen that the
proponents’ ownrouting engineer disclaimed. Joshua Rhodestestified that he made “utilizing Link
U3” his step-one filter—applied before any paralleling or property-line analysis—-which by itself
removes Route 894 and every route except the twelve that use Link U3.'7 Rhodes conceded that,
had the routes instead been weighed on thestatutory factors, his analysis would not have eliminated

Route 894 and that screening on U3 was his “personal preference.” However, he never placed

Naruna Intervenors’ Reply Brief — Page 4 of 7

 Route 392 and Route 894 side by side. !8 Every route that survives the U3 screen carries Segment

U1 across the Naruna ranch, including Route 392.19 The screen is a Segment U1 filter in disguise.

Second, weighed on the statutory factors as the rule requires, Route 392 is plainly inferior
to the non-U1 routes. On the Applicants’ own comparison table, Route 392 is longer than Route
894 (229.02 versus 223.17 miles) and burdens 136 habitable structures within 500 feet against 85
for Route 894—roughly 60% more—at higher cost ($1.737 billion versus $1.681 billion).?° The
U3 Landowners confirm the broader pattern: every filed U3 route—each of which carries Segment
U1—costs more and affects more habitable structures than Route 894.7! A route that sites the line
across 60% more homes, at greater length and cost, while paralleling less existing compatible

right-of-way, does not best meet the prudent-avoidance and paralleling criteria.
D. Reply to Staten Creek Ranch

In its closing brief, Staten Creek Ranch urges the Commission to “place significant weight”
on the fact that “the Northern Corridor routes would pass the furthest from Colorado Bend and
Post Oak Ridge State Parks, and would avoid any impact to those parks.”?* Staten Creek Ranch’s
interpretation is not supported by statute or policy, but merely their self-interest. In consideration
of aesthetic values and environmental integrity, PURA does not state a preference of view line in
state parks over view lines of family ranches. In other words, the harm from visual impacts from
a transmission line in Post Oak Ridge State Park is no more compelling than visual impact on
privately-owned land. But worse, in order to make its argument to reduce fragmentation in
undisturbed park areas, Staten Creek Ranch is necessarily advocating (at cross purposes) for
fragmentation of undisturbed area somewhere else — just away from their ranch. In order to cross
the Colorado River where Staten Creek Ranch proposes, the line must follow U1 and U3 which is
included in the least paralleling corridor.

21 Initial Brief of U3 Landowners at 1; Rowntree Direct at 7, 22 (U3L-1).

22 Staten Creek Ranch’s Initia] Brief at 33.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
Naruna Intervenors’ Reply Brief — Page 5 of 7

 Ill. CONCLUSION

The initial briefs reveal a genuine dispute among the routes but the one proposition on
which the record is unanimous is that no party contends that Segment U1 best meets the routing
criteria.23 Whether the ALJs ultimately recommend Route 894, Route 487, Route 296, Route 572,
or another filed non-U1 route, it can grant the Naruna Intervenors’ requested relief at no cost to
length, cost, reliability, or route adequacy. The disagreement among the proponents is a reason to
resolve the one point that is not in dispute that Segment U1 is inferior under the routing criteria

and should be rejected.

Naruna Intervenors respectfully request that the ALJs issue a Proposal for Decision (1)
rejecting Segment U1 and every route containing Segment U1, including Routes 392, 402, 410,
and 416 and the remaining routes 4K Land and Cattle endorses (Routes 391, 589, 592, 74, 93, and
100); (2) recommending Route 894, Route 487, or another filed route that avoids Segment Ul
entirely; and (3) granting any such further relief to which they may be entitled.

Respectfully submitted,
